Here is the commit message:
arm64: dts: meson-gxbb-wetek: fix HDMI in early boot

Mark the VDDIO_AO18 regulator always-on and set hdmi-supply for the hdmi_tx
node to ensure HDMI is powered in the early stages of boot.

Fixes: fb72c03e0e32 ("ARM64: dts: meson-gxbb-wetek: add a wetek specific dtsi to cleanup hub and play2")

Signed-off-by: Christian Hewitt <christianshewitt@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Neil Armstrong <narmstrong@baylibre.com>
Signed-off-by: Neil Armstrong <narmstrong@baylibre.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20211012052522.30873-2-christianshewitt@gmail.com

Here is the root cause:
The HDMI transmitter (`hdmi_tx`) was not receiving power during the early stages of boot because the associated regulator (`vddio_ao18`) was not configured to be always-on, leading to potential HDMI functionality issues at startup.

Here is the patch:
 		regulator-min-microvolt = <1800000>;
 		regulator-max-microvolt = <1800000>;
+		regulator-always-on;
 	};
 
 	pinctrl-0 = <&hdmi_hpd_pins>, <&hdmi_i2c_pins>;
 	pinctrl-names = "default";
+	hdmi-supply = <&vddio_ao18>;
 };

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```plaintext
regulator-min-microvolt = <1800000>;
regulator-max-microvolt = <1800000>;
```
Reason:
The HDMI transmitter (`hdmi_tx`) was not receiving power during the early stages of boot because the regulator for the HDMI supply (`vddio_ao18`) was not set to be always-on, which meant it could be turned off during boot, leading to HDMI functionality issues.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```plaintext
regulator-always-on;
hdmi-supply = <&vddio_ao18>;
```
Reason:
By adding `regulator-always-on`, the regulator is configured to remain powered on during the early boot stages, ensuring that the HDMI transmitter receives the necessary power. Additionally, setting `hdmi-supply` to `<&vddio_ao18>` explicitly links the HDMI transmitter to the power supply, ensuring it is correctly powered during boot.
